title: PingOne admin and identity provider changes
volume: None on a normal day. Each rule takes one audit activity for one admin change, so an environment sees a few a month, most of them admins at work.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Three custom detection rules for PingOne, on the CloudAudit records the library's PingOne parsers write from PingOne's audit activities. They make a detection when someone assigns a role, adds or changes an external identity provider, or changes or deletes an MFA policy. Each rule matches sensor type PingOne only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's PingOne parsers and point a PingOne webhook at HTTP Ingest first, as the parser entry's README says, then run the check-your-data search to see audit activities arrive.

How it works:
- The parsers write each audit activity's action type, such as ROLE_ASSIGNMENT.CREATED, as the event name, and the admin or app that made the change as the user.
- The role rule takes every role assignment, to a user or an app. PingOne names the role only in the activity's result description, such as Assigned role Environment Admin, so the rule can't tell an admin role from another.
- The identity provider rule takes IDENTITY_PROVIDER.CREATED and IDENTITY_PROVIDER.UPDATED. A new external identity provider can sign users in on PingOne's behalf.
- The MFA rule takes MFA_SETTINGS.UPDATED, and DEVICE_AUTHENTICATION_POLICY.UPDATED and DELETED, the Auth Method Policy changes that set which MFA methods a sign-on accepts.

Tuning:
- If an app assigns roles through the API as part of onboarding, leave it out in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'HR Provisioning'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that account as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-23, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 6 records agreed. The samples went in with their dates moved to the day before the test, so they fell inside the search's time range.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines. Lines sent in the first 12 minutes after the rules were made made no detection on the role rule; sent again about 30 minutes after, they did.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only a sample sign-on on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.

Known gaps:
- A user's MFA device deleted (DEVICE.DELETED) isn't taken: people delete one each time they change phones.
- Sign-ins that skip MFA after a policy change are Auth records, which rules/ping-identity/pingone-mfa-check-failures reads for failures only.
